clue.text: Browning's feeling in April, indoors with 'flu?

blocks.note: indoors is at home
having the flu is a sickness

explanation.surface: A poet laid up indoors with influenza one spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning's poem 'Home-Thoughts, from Abroad' opens 'Oh, to be in England now that April's there', a longing for his country.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning, abroad in Italy, wrote of longing for England in spring, which is pining for one's own country.

clue.text: Woman cut by a piece of wood - find iodine

definitions.note: iodine is an example of the class, not a synonym

indicators.note: something cut by another thing has that thing driven into its middle

blocks.note: hen is slang for a woman
a, plus log for a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A woman wounded by a plank, told to go and find iodine for the cut.
explanation.walkthrough: HEN split by A LOG gives H-ALOG-EN. Iodine sounds like the antiseptic for her wound, but here it is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine belongs to the group of elements, along with fluorine, chlorine and bromine, that chemists call by this name.

clue.text: Not one involved in plan to get high position in Navy

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are knotted into a new order
in places the tangled letters inside the following word

blocks.note: a map is a plan of an area
not as written, plus I for one

explanation.surface: Someone excluded from a scheme to win a senior naval post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not one' reads as 'nobody', but it is two pieces of fodder, with one standing for the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: The maintop is a platform at the head of a sailing ship's mainmast, literally a lofty station aboard a warship.

clue.text: Gun Caesar into bits in the long grass

indicators.note: blowing something into bits scatters its pieces, which then reassemble differently

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Shooting Julius Caesar to pieces while hiding in tall grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar cane is a tall tropical plant of the grass family grown for its sweet stems.

clue.text: Get European to stop talking

indicators.note: talking means we hear the word spoken rather than see it written

blocks.note: to check is to halt or stop

explanation.surface: Telling a chatty foreigner to stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop talking' looks like a command to be quiet; instead 'talking' signals that the word for 'stop' is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A Czech is a native of the Czech lands, Bohemia and Moravia, in central Europe.

clue.text: First-class event, moving in its simplicity

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about into a new sequence

blocks.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for a top-class occasion that touches the heart by being simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' reads as touching, but it signals the shuffle of A1 and EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent artlessness, an unsophisticated lack of worldly guile.

clue.text: Young Werther's often spoken of as being drowned

definitions.text: often spoken of as being drowned

blocks.note: Goethe's novel is The ... of Young Werther

blocks.clueFragment: often spoken of as being drowned
blocks.note: people say they are drowning their troubles in drink

explanation.surface: Goethe's hero is often said to have met his end by drowning.
explanation.walkthrough: Werther in fact shoots himself; the drowning belongs to the idiom about drink, not to the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Goethe titled his novel after the young man's griefs, and the same griefs are what a drinker tries to drown.

clue.text: Preacher in Northern town is about to turn east

indicators.note: to turn here means the word rotates, its first letter moving round to the back
about means going around, so the two letters wrap round the rotated word

blocks.note: Eccles is a town near Manchester in northern England
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman in a northern town is about to head east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to turn east' reads as 'on the point of heading east'; 'about' is actually a container signal and 'turn' a rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament book's Hebrew title Koheleth is traditionally rendered 'the Preacher', its supposed author.

clue.text: About exhausted by end of gruelling vocation

indicators.note: end of tells us to keep only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
all in is a phrase for exhausted
the last letter of gruelling

explanation.surface: Someone nearly worn out by the close of a punishing career.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a profession one feels drawn to, a strong inner summons to some kind of work.

clue.text: Martial art in verse, for example

definitions.text: Martial art in verse, for example

blocks.note: surface reading: a fighting discipline such as karate

blocks.clueFragment: Martial art in verse, for example
blocks.note: setter's reading: Martial was a Roman poet, and his art was a short witty poem

explanation.surface: A fighting skill described in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Martial, capitalised at the start, is the Roman poet famous for barbed short poems, not the adjective of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial's chosen form was the brief, pointed, witty poem, and his twelve books of them defined the genre.

clue.text: Spider that can make one Audi

definitions.note: a description of what makes money, enough to buy a car

blocks.note: first meaning: the tiny money spider, said to bring good fortune
second meaning: a venture so profitable it could buy a German car

explanation.walkthrough: A money spider is a tiny spider said to bring wealth to whoever it lands on; another name for it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the lucky little spider and any highly profitable business venture or product.

clue.text: The barge, when unloaded?

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat-bottomed boat for ferrying cargo
second meaning: weighing less after the cargo is taken off

explanation.surface: What the barge becomes once its cargo is off.
explanation.definitionFit: The boat used to ferry goods to and from ships shares its name with the comparative of not heavy.

clue.text: Gardening finished, have a dance

blocks.note: to hoe is to do gardening with a weeding tool
down as in done, over

explanation.surface: The garden work is done, so time for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American country dance, or a social gathering held for such dancing.

clue.text: Internationalists in New York go in to eat early

definitions.note: adverb for a noun; at sunup means early

indicators.note: go in asks one word to enter and sit inside the other

blocks.note: sup is an old word meaning to eat or dine
the United Nations, headquartered in New York

explanation.surface: Diplomats in Manhattan heading off for an early meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In New York' is not a container signal; it just identifies which internationalists are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is dawn, the hour of sunrise, and doing something at that hour is doing it early.

clue.text: Cockney speaking cruelly but naturally

indicators.note: a Cockney famously drops the initial aitch when speaking

blocks.note: acting heartlessly is acting cruelly

explanation.surface: A Londoner who talks cruelly but without affectation.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are Londoners whose accent drops initial H, so HEARTLESSLY loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Artlessly means without guile or affectation, in an unstudied and spontaneous way.

clue.text: Vied at law to get order changed; naturally, it was a disaster

indicators.note: if the order is changed, these letters come in a different sequence

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal battle meant to change a rule ended in catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naturally' is part of the definition: a natural disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge sea surge, often from an undersea earthquake, is a catastrophe caused by nature rather than people.

clue.text: Go in fear of arrest

blocks.note: first meaning: to dread or anticipate with anxiety
second meaning: to seize and take into custody

explanation.surface: Being afraid of getting nicked by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both anxious foreboding, as in apprehension, and police seizing a suspect.

clue.text: Order about mountain climbing may bring psychological benefit

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: the Order of the British Empire
c for circa, about
an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: Mountaineering on doctor's orders may be good for the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE, C and ALP, read upwards as a whole, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill with no active drug can still make patients feel better simply because they believe in it.

clue.text: Building is English if covered in cubes

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: E abbreviates English
dice are cubes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Speculating whether an English building would be clad in cubes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If' is not a conditional here; it is taken literally as two letters to be enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing building or structure.

clue.text: Sum up about start of cereal harvest

indicators.note: start of keeps only the opening letter of the next word
about means surrounding, so one word goes round the selected letter

blocks.note: to reap is to harvest a crop
the first letter of cereal

explanation.surface: Totalling the cereal crop at the start of the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to recapitulate, briefly restating the main points of what has been said.

clue.text: Farcical occasion to support university fund-raising

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so it is written after

blocks.note: rag week is the British students' annual charity fund-raising
an occasion is a time

explanation.surface: A silly event held to back a college charity drive.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities, rag is the students' yearly round of stunts and collections for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the word as an adjective meaning ridiculous or not to be taken seriously, beside its sense of syncopated piano music.

clue.text: Sophisticated worker creates lubricant

definitions.note: a coolant often doubles as a lubricant in machining

blocks.note: cool means stylish or sophisticated
the worker ant

explanation.surface: A suave labourer produces a slippery oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting fluids in machine shops both cool the tool and lubricate it, so the fluid serves either role.

clue.text: Dresses in informal shirts belonging to the Emperor

indicators.note: in places the first word between the letters of the second

blocks.note: tees, informal shirts, written as two Ts
saris are Indian dresses

explanation.surface: Casual clothes and gowns that were the Emperor's own.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsarist means relating to the tsar, the Russian emperor, or to his autocratic rule.

clue.text: Wooden soldiers - there's a number about

indicators.note: about means around, so a number goes round the soldiers

blocks.note: ten is a number
the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A box of toy soldiers, with a number lying about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden soldiers' looks like one phrase, but 'Wooden' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Treen, an old word, describes things made of wood, especially small turned household items.

clue.text: Instrument on stage sounds foul

definitions.note: a sound-alike for fowl, the bird

indicators.note: on means placed after, the first item set on top of the next

blocks.note: a leg is a stage of a journey
a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A musical instrument on stage that makes a horrible noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds foul' seems to judge the instrument; it means a word pronounced like fowl, the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leghorn is a breed of domestic chicken originating near Livorno in Italy.

clue.text: Unable to bear being completely clean

blocks.note: first meaning: unable to have children
second meaning: free of germs

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot stand being spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to bear' reads as unable to tolerate; here bear means give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers infertility and also total freedom from bacteria, as in a hospital operating theatre.

clue.text: Lively bird echoed a note

indicators.note: an echo comes back, so the bird's name is sent backwards

blocks.note: mina is a variant spelling of myna, the Asian starling
taken as written
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A cheerful bird repeating a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: MINA reversed gives ANIM, then A and TE.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, animate means alive or full of life, the opposite of inanimate.

clue.text: Cease to care because the Principal works inefficiently?

blocks.note: first meaning: to become bored or indifferent
second meaning: capital badly invested earns no return

explanation.surface: Giving up caring because the headteacher is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: Principal looks like a head of college, but in finance it is the capital sum on which returns are paid.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means growing indifferent, and literally describes money failing to earn its yearly return.
